title: Book One · Chapter 120: A Small Table
story:
Dad looks at the side space after work. He asks Ronan to stay outside the little door. Then he checks the roof and the shelf.

“May I hold the light?” Ronan asks.

“From the yard. Stay here.”

Dad points to a place. Ronan holds the small lamp there. It makes a round bright place on the wood.

“Higher.”

Ronan lifts his arm.

“That is the roof outside,” Dad says. “A little lower.”

Mum comes past with their bowls.

“If you find our dinner up there, bring it down.”

Dad checks the low shelf too. He puts one hand on it, then both. It moves.

“No books on this one.”

Mr Qiu looks unhappy. “Only the light boxes?”

“Not yet. This end needs work.”

Mrs Lan brings out a key. “Then we use the high shelf for now. I can move my empty baskets.”

Dad checks that shelf. It is fixed to a different wall. He asks Mrs Lan about the roof above it. She points to the wet place from last year. Then she shows him the dry part.

Ronan listens. He has lived in the yard for a long time now. He did not know rain came in there last year. Mrs Lan remembers the wet places.

“Dry things only,” Dad says at last. “And small boxes. Someone must pass them up to an adult.”

Mr Qiu rubs his hands together.

“I have small boxes.”

“You have boxes inside boxes,” Mrs Lan says.

They bring out the narrow board. Two old wooden stands belong to Mrs Lan. Dad looks at them and puts one aside. One leg is split.

Ronan runs to their kitchen for the little table. Mum still needs that table. Ronan must ask her first. He stops at the kitchen door.

“Mum, may we try our table?”

She looks at the bowls on it.

“For a look, yes. For three days, no. We eat here.”

The table fits the marks. It shows them the right size. Dad takes a piece of paper and writes two numbers on it for Mr Qiu.

“Ask Mr Sun tomorrow. There may be an old table at the back. Mr Sun may sell it. I must ask him. I cannot give you his things.”

“I can pay something,” Mr Qiu says.

“Ask the price first.”

When their table is back in the kitchen, Ronan's rice is a little cold. He eats it anyway. Dad sits down slowly and rubs his neck.

“Did we help?” Ronan asks.

“We know more than we did this morning.”

“But there is no table.”

“There is dinner,” Mum says. “On a table.”

Ronan looks at his bowl. He smiles.

Later he writes the two numbers again on Mr Qiu's paper. He makes them large and clear. Then he puts the paper in a dry envelope. He writes Mr Qiu's name on the front. He can finish this job tonight.

Before bed he shows Mum the envelope. She reads both numbers. “Which number is the width?” she asks. Ronan looks at the paper. He cannot tell. He takes it back to Dad and asks. Dad draws a little table beside the numbers. Ronan copies the two short lines onto the envelope too. He reads both numbers with Dad once more. Now Mr Qiu can show them to Mr Sun. He can show the real sizes tomorrow.

He puts it by his shoes. That way he can remember it in the morning. Then he moves his shoes away from the door, so Mum can come in.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：for a look＝拿来看看；split＝裂开；ask the price＝询问价格。

情节提示：envelope＝信封；width＝宽度；shelf＝架子。

理解：1. 为什么不能把小厨房的桌子给 Mr Qiu 用三天？2. Ronan 当晚完成了什么小事？
